listing_name: Historic Icelandic Cottage Meets Urban Elegance
description:
Discover our classic stone cottage in Reykjavik's historic district. Adorned with local art and musical instruments, it's an Icelandic cultural immersion. Experience the serenity of a country home, yet steps away from the city's attractions. Welcome to our Icelandic oasis.

The space
Nestled in the heart of Reykjavik's picturesque historic district, our enchanting stone cottage seamlessly blends traditional Icelandic charm with contemporary luxury. As one of the capital's time-honored structures, every corner of this cottage whispers tales of yesteryears while offering the comforts and amenities of the modern world.

A mere 5-minute stroll from your doorstep places you amidst the vibrant city center, bustling with chic boutiques, immersive museums, and delightful eateries that promise a taste of Iceland's rich culinary tapestry.

Inside, the cottage reveals two bedrooms, exuding warmth and coziness. The stylish open-concept space beckons with a plush lounge sofa, perfect for evening relaxation. For the culinary enthusiast, a fully-equipped kitchen awaits, crowned with a sleek Nespresso machine to kickstart your mornings. The contemporary bathroom, complete with a bathtub/shower combo and a state-of-the-art washer/dryer unit, ensures your utmost convenience.

Accentuated by private parking, an exclusive entrance, and its unbeatable central location, this cottage is more than just a place to stay; it's an experience, an Icelandic embrace. With our unwavering commitment to your comfort, we aim to make your sojourn in Reykjavik nothing short of unforgettable.

Guest access
Everything is included.

description:
Apartment in central Reykjavík, cozy, with charm and great view of the kitchen-clock-church Hallgrímskyrkja, the bay and Reykjavikers favorite mountain Esjan. The space

Kitchen and living room are in one cozy space, both are fully implemented. The Kitchen has a refrigerator, freezer, stove, oven, toaster, kettle, blender..., dishwasher, cooking utensils and tableware...

listing_name: A 'Church' in the heart of town
description:
A beautiful private house by a quiet street, right in the middle of Reykjavík. Various bedrooms, single beds, double beds and an idyllic garden.

The space
This beautifully restored house is in a quiet street, right in the centre of Reykjavík! It is designed in 1925 by a church builder - and is known as the 'Church', although it never served as such.

The house accommodates six people, ideally a couple with children, but there is easily room for more people. The house is 120m2, on two floors. The kitchen is on the ground floor and so is the living room - directly connected to the very sunny and beautiful garden. There is one bedroom on the ground floor. On the first floor is a bedroom with a big double bed, two children's bedrooms and a spacious bright bathroom. And there is room for two people to sleep in the attic.

The main shopping streets are literally just around the corner - with a great variety of cafés, restaurants, galleries, museums etc. in the neighbourhood. The main bus terminal and a swimming pool are less than a 10 minutes walk - and the well known Reykjavik landmark, the church Hallgrímskirkja, can be seen from the living room window.

Linen, towels, hair dryer, iron and other features are in place. There is a washing machine, free of charge Wi-Fi Intenet connection.... - and very important; a parking space.

I would love to inform you all I know about the city and the country, about the people and the culture - I travel quite a lot around Iceland, so hopefully I could be of some help.

Guest access
The guests have access to the whole house, the garden and the washing room. Occasionally I stay in a small building, overlooking the same garden - connected by the washing room. That building has a separate entrance.

Luxurious, spacious apartment in the embassy district, one of Reykjavík’s most desirable areas. Across from a beautiful park, with private patio and separate entrance. Just a 2-minute walk to the City Hall and Bus Stop #1 for day tours such as the Golden Circle, South Coast, Whale Watching, Northern Lights, and more.

description:
Niel's room, as we call it, is a large double room with a king-sized bed. It also has an additional single, so can be made up for a couple with a child or as three single beds for a small group.
We offer it for a slightly reduced cost because it is on the bottom floor, but interestingly is often requested by our regular visitors, of whom we have many, because it is discrete, snug, has good blackout blinds, and has a nice aspect out into the garden.

The space
The house is a traditional timber built Icelandic house, warm and snug throughout the year as heated with Iceland’s famous hydro-thermic hot water. All our guests have access to three shared bathrooms, two sitting rooms, an office space upstairs, a dining area, and to a kitchen which can be used for heating up food and snacks but not for cooking full meals. We do not offer breakfast for the very good reasons that we are not licenced to serve food and there are so many excellent bakeries, restaurants and coffee houses so locally; these open very early.
Our house itself is well known, and is listed. Built in 1906, it was a bicycle shop for fifty years, the first of these in Iceland, and as such it is much loved in Reykjavik, especially by people who bought their first bike here a generation ago. We are popular with film companies who love filming here. Traditional timber framed houses have certain features and quirks. Ours flexes and breathes, which is important in earthquake prone zones like ours, but it does mean that it is not as soundproof as modern concrete buildings are.

Guest access
Your private bedroom, two sitting rooms, a small office space upstairs, kitchen and dining room. There are three shared bathrooms which guests can use exclusively. There is a back yard with attractive golden rowan trees in it which is a nice aspect out of the windows, but this is part of our family space and not part of the guesthouse strictly speaking.

During your stay
I am half English / half Icelandic, born and bred in Reykjavik, and am native in both languages. This is my home as I grew a couple of hundred meters away in Njalsgata street. My husband Fergus is Anglo-Irish and our children (by upbringing) are English. Our part of the property is adjacent to but attached to the guesthouse. We are in residence most of the time, but spend some time in England as two of our now adult children live there. When not here, we have a manager who lives in.
Be in touch before you travel to allow us to help you have the best possible experience of Iceland. Once you book we will send you directions and instructions for a stress free arrival.

Other things to note
Reykjavik is served by hydro-thermally heated water. Our hot water is hot and plentiful therefore and each bedroom has a radiator with an adjustable regulator. Don't be cold. Turn your radiator up if you wish.
Hydro-thermic hot water is, by definition, volcanic, and therefore very slightly sulphurous. It is good for your skin. It tastes a bit off however, so run the mixer tap on cold for a good few seconds before drinking it or brushing your teeth. We have the best quality municipal drinking water in the world, by a very considerable margin. Delicious.

We are a licenced, family run, and fantastically well located guesthouse in the centre of Reykjavik 101.

The space
The house is a traditional timber built Icelandic house, warm and snug throughout the year as heated with Iceland’s famous hydro-thermic hot water. All our guests have access to three shared bathrooms, two sitting rooms, an office space upstairs, a dining area, and to a kitchen which can be used for heating up food and snacks but not for cooking full meals. Your private bedroom, two sitting rooms, a small office space upstairs, kitchen and dining room. There are three shared bathrooms which guests can use exclusively. I am half English / half Icelandic, born and bred in Reykjavik, and am native in both languages. This is my home as I grew a couple of hundred meters away in Njalsgata street. It tastes a bit off however, so run the mixer tap on cold for a good few seconds before drinking it or brushing your teeth. We have the best quality municipal drinking water in the world, by a very considerable margin. Delicious.

listing_name: Dollhouse in the heart of Reykjavik
description:
In the center of old Reykjavik (right next to Hallgrimskirkja Church), this charming 2 bedroom house is a unique find in the perfect location. With less than a 5 minutes walk to the main shopping street you will be as close as possible to all the main sights, restaurants and shopping that Reykjavik city center has to offer, yet just far enough for a good night's sleep in a quiet, residential area.

The space
Please keep in mind that this is my own home, so you will be living like a local in a personalized space, not a generic apartment.

The house is one of the classic, Icelandic corrugated iron houses. Built in 1927, it is listed as one of cultural value, because it is an example of the typical Reykjavík streetscape of the early 20th century. It is situated in a courtyard and not visible from the street, which means that it is very peaceful and quiet despite being so close to the buzz of downtown. This house has a lot of soul, and I kindly ask you to treat it with care ❤️

There is a minimarket (Krambudin) with essentials two blocks away, open until late. A grocery store (Krónan) is also within walking distance. Across the street you will find an excellent wood-fire pizzeria and a plethora of other restaurants, bakeries and bars etc are within easy walking distance. The local swimming pool Sundhöllin is less than 10 minutes walk away.

Guest access
The entire house is available to you, with two private entrances (one on each floor). One bedroom has a queen size bed, the other room has 2 single beds which can be pushed together to make a double. The bathroom has a shower + bath tub.

The two bedrooms and bathroom are on the ground-floor, while the upper floor has a small kitchen, dining room and living room with tv. Outside there is a small courtyard, with a small table and chairs, which enjoys sunshine until mid-afternoon during summer.

Parking: The street is at the end of the paid parking zone (P3), meaning that there is free parking just around the corner, within 1 minute walking distance. In my street, there is a fee between 9am-6pm on weekdays, while the weekends are free.

Other things to note
Please be aware that the kitchen is small and unfortunately has no dishwasher, but it is otherwise well equipped.

Free public parking across the street.

The space
The apartment is located in a friendly neighborhood in the old part of the residential city center. It is only 950 meters from the city center itself and 600 meters from Grandi harbor, which up until recently, was limited to anything “fishy”. However, over the past couple of years, the area has evolved into a fantastic conglomeration of restaurants, shops, museums, and IT businesses, as well as fishing boats and baiting huts. Grandi is literally teeming with life. There are small fishing boats regularly coming into the harbor to land their catch, and then there is the dry dock where bigger trawlers are being repaired. The scenery isn't half bad either— there´s the panoramic view out over Faxaflói bay and Mount Esja rises majestically in the distance. The invigorating smell of the sea, the views, eateries, boutiques, cultural activities, and the hustle and bustle of this fashionable part of town make it an ideal place for a leisurely stroll, coffee, shops, and the newest ice cream shop (Italian ice) in Reykjavík. It is very close to the harbor and the city center. Everything is very close to our place so the best way to travel around our neighborhood is by foot or bike. But the Bus Terminal is just ca. 25 min. walking from our place.

listing_name: The Old Bicycle Shop  - Twin room
description:
Eva’s room (named after our daughter whose bedroom it once was), is a small twin room with two 90cm beds. It is ideal for friends, siblings, or parent and offspring. It's aspect is over Spitalastigur.
We are a licenced, family run, and fantastically well located guesthouse in the centre of Reykjavik 101. All Reykjavik’s main attractions, including her best restaurants, bars, cafes, sites and museums are within a few hundred meters, and the city’s festivals and events happen on our doorstep.

The space
The house is a traditional timber built Icelandic house, warm and snug throughout the year as heated with Iceland’s famous hydro-thermic hot water. All our guests have access to three shared bathrooms, two sitting rooms, an office space upstairs, a dining area, and to a kitchen which can be used for heating up food and snacks but not for cooking full meals. We do not offer breakfast for the very good reasons that we are not licenced to serve food and there are so many excellent bakeries, restaurants and coffee houses so locally; these open very early.
Our house itself is well known, and is listed. Built in 1906, it was a bicycle shop for fifty years, the first of these in Iceland, and as such it is much loved in Reykjavik, especially by people who bought their first bike here a generation ago. We are popular with film companies who love filming here. Traditional timber framed houses have certain features and quirks. Ours flexes and breathes, which is important in earthquake prone zones like ours, but it does mean that it is not as soundproof as modern concrete buildings are.

Guest access
Your private bedroom, sitting room, kitchen, and dining room. There is a shared bathroom on every floor. The kitchen is suitable for teas and coffees, light snacks and heating up simple foods, but we do not allow cooking. There is a back yard with attractive golden rowan trees in it which is a nice aspect out of the windows, but this is part of our family space and not part of the guesthouse strictly speaking.

During your stay
I am half English / half Icelandic, born and bred in Reykjavik, and am native in both languages. This is my home as I grew a couple of hundred meters away in Njalsgata street. My husband Fergus is Anglo-Irish and our children (by upbringing) are English. Our part of the property is adjacent to but attached to the guesthouse. We are in residence most of the time, but spend some time in England as our now adult children live there. When not here, we have a manager who lives in.
Be in touch before you travel to allow us to help you have the best possible experience of Iceland. Once you book we will send you directions and instructions for a stress free arrival.

Other things to note
